requirements.text: An effect is described by its manifest (effect.json) alone: its identity, version, label, entry module, styles, preview, the surfaces it may be chosen for, the schemes it draws, its pair, its capabilities, its settings, what it needs and, optionally, the homepage where its author shows it. A product lists, describes and configures it -- building the settings form from the manifest's settings with its record view, never a form per effect -- without running its code.
requirements.guidance: SF.Effects.checkEffectManifest; the kit's manifest check. Since 1.1 this requirement also holds what 1.0 stated as settings-form-from-the-manifest. Since 1.4 the manifest may name homepage (effect manifest schema 1.4.0): an http or https address without credentials.

requirements.text: Every setting has a key, a property type (choice, integer, number, boolean, string, text, color, file), a label and a valid default; numbers state their bounds, strings their longest length, choices their options, files the kinds of the site's files they accept. A setting may be conditional: its when names another setting of the same effect (key) and the values that setting must hold (is); it is shown and read only while that setting, itself read, holds one of them. The key is never the setting itself, the conditions form no loop, and every value listed is a valid value of the setting named -- for a choice, one of its options.
requirements.guidance: Manifest field settings[].when = {key, is} (effect manifest schema 1.3.0, since simai.effect 1.3). SF.Effects.checkEffectManifest and the kit's manifest check refuse a when whose key names no setting or the setting itself, a value that is not among the options of a choice (or not a valid value of another type), and a loop of conditions.

requirements.text: A product checks every stored value against its setting before saving it and before handing it to the effect; an invalid or missing value is replaced by the default, never passed on. A conditional setting whose condition is false is not read at all: its stored value is ignored, its default is not applied, and the effect is given no value for it; a settings form shows it only while its condition holds.
requirements.guidance: SF.Effects.effectSettings answers the checked settings and names the keys it dropped; since 1.3 it leaves out the key of a setting whose condition is false (and does not name it as dropped), so the keys it answers for the values on a form are the settings that form shows.

requirements.text: The entry is one module exporting mount(host, settings, context), answering update, pause, resume and destroy. New settings, and a change of the scheme it draws in, reach a mounted effect through update(settings, context); it redraws without being mounted again.
requirements.guidance: context carries reducedMotion, locale and, since 1.1, scheme. Since 1.1 this requirement also holds what 1.0 stated as update-without-remount.

requirements.text: An effect draws only inside its host, at a pixel density of at most 2: it adds its own canvas or video there and touches nothing else on the page.
requirements.guidance: Since 1.1 this requirement also holds what 1.0 stated as pixel-density-capped.

requirements.text: An effect makes no requests (needs.network is false in version 1): no fetch, no image or script from outside its own files and the site's files its settings name.
requirements.guidance: The kit fails an effect that asks for anything beyond its own files.

requirements.text: With reduced motion an effect draws one still frame and stops asking for frames; a person who turns reduced motion on is given the still frame at once.
While the tab is hidden an effect draws nothing and asks for no frames.

The host is out of the accessibility tree (aria-hidden) and takes no pointer events: an effect stands under the page's controls, never over them. A placement may answer a right-click on the effect's own background -- where nothing but the effect is under the pointer -- with a small menu that names the effect, its version and author, links to its page in the catalogue (or to the homepage its manifest names) and pauses or resumes its motion as the placement's own pause does. A right-click on content over the effect, a right-click with Shift, and a right-click where the site turned the menu off keep the browser's own menu; the menu adds nothing to the tab order or to what a screen reader reads, and costs a page nothing until it is first opened.
requirements.guidance: SF.Effects places the menu with every placement (placeEffect, data-sf-effect, mountEffect with a theme mode, mountWindows); SF_BOOT_CONFIG.effects.about = false turns it off for the page and data-sf-effect-about="false" for an area or anything inside it. The probe effect-about covers it inline, in windows mode and over a foreign effect's sandbox frame.

requirements.text: After destroy an effect has left nothing behind -- no nodes, frames, observers or listeners -- and it can be mounted again.

An effect declares the schemes it is drawn for -- dark, light or both, its home scheme first -- and each scheme is designed for its own ground, not an inverted picture; no schemes means both, as in 1.0. A single-scheme effect may name a pair: the effect of the other scheme that plays the same role, given as a catalogue id or the https address of its effect.json.
requirements.guidance: Manifest fields schemes and pair (effect manifest schema 1.2.0). Declare a pair for every single-scheme effect meant for public pages, unless no effect of the other scheme can play its role.

requirements.text: A placement has a theme mode: as the page (auto, the default), always dark or always light. When the effect cannot draw the target scheme, its pair is shown; failing a pair, in auto a single-scheme effect keeps its own scheme: a dark-only effect stays dark on a light page and a light-only effect stays light on a dark page, its area in that scheme. A fixed mode the effect cannot draw shows a plain surface of that theme instead. An editor offers only the fixed modes the effect, or its pair, can draw.
requirements.guidance: The resolution order: the effect in the target scheme; its pair in the target scheme; in auto, a single-scheme effect in its own scheme; nothing (a fixed mode it cannot draw). SF.Effects.resolveTheme carries it.

requirements.text: The area of an effect takes the theme it is actually drawn in (theme-dark or theme-light), whatever the page's theme, so text and controls over it use that theme's roles. At the manifest's default settings, on the effect's brightest frame, the primary text role measures at least 4.5:1 and the dimmed text role at least 3:1. Dimmed text over an effect is therefore large text (24px, or 18.66px bold), as WCAG allows at 3:1; small text over an effect takes the primary role. A person who raises a setting past its default owns the contrast that results; the defaults are what an effect promises.
requirements.guidance: The kit's contrast check: --sf-on-surface at 4.5:1 and --sf-on-surface-variant at 3:1, over the worst of five frames, at the 5th percentile of the pixels, with every setting at its default (owner decision, 2026-10-19).

requirements.text: An effect draws with palette tones (--sf-<palette>-<tone>, such as --sf-primary-40 or --sf-neutral-98), which stay the same across themes and carry the project's colours, chosen per scheme by the effect itself; it does not draw with theme roles, which change under it with the area's theme and may not exist at all.
requirements.guidance: The effects lab found every one of its first twenty effects reading --sf-surface, a role core does not define. Read a tone through a short-lived probe element so var() chains and light-dark() settle; keep a fallback colour for a page without the Framework's sheets; read the tones again when the theme or project colours change.

requirements.text: An effect that declares the windows capability may be drawn once behind a group of cards and seen only through them: it draws one continuous scene over the whole group, follows the group's size, and relies on nothing the mask hides; every other rule still holds. Only cards that are windows take the effect's theme; the others keep the page's.
requirements.guidance: Manifest capabilities: ["windows"]. The kit draws it behind three window cards under a mask, at two widths, and fails it when anything shows outside the windows or the scene does not span the group.

requirements.text: An effect that fails to mount or throws is replaced by the product's default effect, and the failure is reported (sf-effect-error), never shown to the person as a broken page.

An effect not shipped and reviewed with a product runs only in an iframe sandboxed without allow-same-origin, under a strict content security policy, receiving its checked settings by message: it can never reach the page, its cookies or a form on it.

A pair is resolved and loaded under the same trust as any effect. An id resolves against the catalogue base and is checked against that catalogue index's SHA-256 before it runs inline; an address outside the pinned catalogue is foreign and runs only in the sandbox runner, and is refused while there is none. A trusted effect never pulls an untrusted pair inline.
requirements.guidance: SF.Effects.pairIsForeign names a pair given as an address; the kit notes such a pair as needing the sandbox.

requirements.text: An effect is installed only after its package is checked -- the files it may hold, its size, its manifest, a digest of every file -- and installed switched off until a person turns it on.

A product runs the kit (scripts/effect-kit.mjs) on an effect before listing it: manifest, defaults, mount, no network, still motion, hidden tab, pixel ratio, update, cleanup, remount, accessibility, and for what the manifest declares, each scheme with its contrast, the scheme switch, the windows mode and the pair's trust.
requirements.guidance: The probe effect-kit runs it on a rule-keeping and a rule-breaking fixture, and on a two-scheme, windows-capable fixture.

uses.description: The form of effect.json: identity, entry, surfaces, schemes, pair, capabilities, typed and bounded settings with their conditions, needs, homepage.

specification.description: Envelope schema, copied from ai-first standard-contract 1.0 at revision 8ed3d48efdb2435f1dd4142ab3339b00f5340fb1.

simai.ownership.scope_note: An animated background drawn into one area of a page -- a sign-in page's art side, a hero block, a group of cards seen as windows. The Framework owns the manifest, the module interface, the runtime rules, the theme policy, SF.Effects and the kit; the catalogue (simai/ui-effects) owns the effects; a product owns its built-in effects, installing and turning effects on, their settings and placements.
simai.ownership.origin: Designed by simai/larena (larena-specs docs/architecture/2026-10-14-background-effects.md, approved by the owner 2026-10-14), the contract handed to the Framework; authored for publication on 2026-10-16. Edition 1.1.0 (2026-10-19) takes the owner's decisions after the gallery review: schemes, pairs, the placement's theme mode and the windows mode in the standard, effects in the separate catalogue simai/ui-effects (ui-control control/handoffs/2026-10-19-effects-core.md; evidence in the effects lab: THEMES.md, SCHEMES.md, 240 combinations at 4.5:1 or more), and the pair's trust agreed with the catalogue owner. Edition 1.2.0 (2026-10-28) takes the owner's decision in the catalogue thread: a light-only effect stays light on a dark page in auto, as a dark-only effect stays dark on a light one. Edition 1.3.0 (2026-11-01) takes the owner's request relayed by the catalogue thread (simai/ui-effects): a setting shown only while another holds certain values, named when with key and is. Edition 1.4.0 (2026-11-02) takes the owner's decision relayed by the catalogue thread: every area an effect is placed in answers a right-click on its background with a small English menu, so a visitor of any site can see what the background is and reach SIMAI Effects.
simai.ownership.changes: 1.4.0 adds the about menu: not-in-the-way says a placement may answer a right-click on the effect's own background with a menu (name and version, author, a link, pause and resume) while content, Shift and a site's switch keep the browser's menu; manifest-describes-everything names the optional homepage, and the pin moves to the effect manifest schema 1.4.0 (homepage; every 1.3 manifest stays valid). No requirement was added or removed. The bytes of 1.3.0 stay in history. Before: 1.3.0 adds conditional settings: settings-are-typed-and-bounded gains the optional when = {key, is} and its checks, values-checked-before-use says a setting whose condition is false is not read, and the pin moves to the effect manifest schema 1.3.0 (settings[].when; every 1.2 manifest stays valid). No requirement was added or removed. The bytes of 1.2.0 stay in history. Before: 1.2.0 changes theme-follows-the-placement: in auto a light-only effect without a pair keeps its light scheme on a dark page instead of being hidden, so both single-scheme cases resolve alike; the reason light-only-on-dark is gone. No other requirement and no pin changed. The bytes of 1.1.0 stay in history. Before: 1.1.0 adds schemes-and-pair-declared, theme-follows-the-placement, area-takes-the-drawn-theme, drawn-with-palette-tones, windows-are-mask-safe and pair-under-the-same-trust, and pins the effect manifest schema 1.2.0 (schemes, pair, capabilities; a 1.0 manifest stays valid). To stay within twenty principles three 1.0 requirements were folded into neighbours with their text kept: settings-form-from-the-manifest into manifest-describes-everything, update-without-remount into one-module-one-mount, pixel-density-capped into draws-in-its-host-only. The module contract gains context.scheme and update(settings, context). The bytes of 1.0.0 stay in history.
validated_against: the kit on a rule-keeping and a rule-breaking fixture (tests/fixtures/effect-sample, effect-bad)
the kit on a two-scheme, windows-capable fixture (tests/fixtures/effect-schemes)
the kit on six effects-lab effects carrying the 1.1 fields: dark-only, light-only, both, a pair by id and a pair by address
the unit test tests/effect-manifest.contract.test.mjs on conditional settings: a choice, a boolean and a chain read and not read, and every refused form of when
the unit test tests/effect-manifest.contract.test.mjs on homepage and the about menu's entries and link
the probe tests/browser/effect-about.browser.mjs: background, text, link, Shift, the page switch and the area switch, pause and resume, inline, windows and sandboxed
